events.title: Prior judicial ruling that Trump-appointed US attorney's appointment violated the Constitution
events.summary: In November 2026, Federal judge Cameron McGowan Currie dismissed prosecutions of James Comey and Letitia James, ruling that Lindsey Halligan's appointment as US attorney was unlawful and violated the Constitution. Currie found that Halligan's predecessor Erik Siebert had already served the required interim period, nullifying her appointment. Currie wrote that "all actions flowing from Ms Halligan's defective appointment" were "unlawful exercises of executive power and must be set aside." The Justice Department appealed but no stay was issued.
events.why_relevant: A federal judge found the Trump administration violated the Constitution by appointing an unqualified lawyer to prosecute political opponents, striking at both rule of law and the separation of powers.
events.basis: Federal judge Cameron McGowan Currie threw out both cases in November, writing in a scathing opinion that Halligan's installation was invalid, and 'all actions flowing from Ms Halligan's defective appointment' were 'unlawful exercises of executive power and must be set aside'.

events.title: Missouri Attorney General announces investigation into referendum support firm alleging undocumented worker hiring
events.summary: In November 2026, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced an investigation into a firm working in support of the redistricting referendum, accusing the company of hiring undocumented workers to gather signatures. Hanaway provided no evidence for the allegations. The announcement was followed by Donald Trump Jr. targeting People Not Politicians executive director Richard von Glahn on social media, claiming he was "trying to STEAL a GOP house seat in Missouri through an unlawful referendum."
events.why_relevant: The unsubstantiated investigation and accompanying social media attacks by a Trump family member constitute a coordinated effort to delegitimize and intimidate the referendum campaign through law enforcement and political pressure.
events.federal_nexus: Donald Trump Jr., a private citizen with federal political influence, amplified the allegations on social media.
events.basis: In November, Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway announced an investigation into a firm working in support of the referendum, accusing the company of hiring undocumented workers to gather signatures. She provided no evidence for those allegations.

events.title: DOJ workforce reduction and prosecutor resignations
events.summary: The Department of Justice workforce dropped by 8% from November 2024 to November 2025, according to US Office of Personnel Management statistics. Veteran prosecutors have resigned or been fired in key offices including Minneapolis, Virginia, and Los Angeles in response to the department's politicization under Trump. Former DOJ Inspector General Michael Bromwich noted that experienced prosecutors could not abide a department run by "political pawns of the White House."
events.why_relevant: Mass departures of experienced prosecutors in response to politicization weaken the DOJ's institutional capacity and credibility, undermining the department's ability to pursue justice impartially.
events.basis: the DoJ's workforce dropped by 8% from November of 2024 to November 2025, according to statistics from the US office of personnel management
